name: Scalp micropigmentation

card.summary: A cosmetic tattoo of tiny pigment dots that mimics a buzzed head or denser hair; it camouflages rather than regrows hair.
card.note: No clinical studies cited; the pigment is semi-permanent to permanent and can be removed by laser.

quick.overview:
Scalp micropigmentation (SMP) is a non-surgical cosmetic tattoo that deposits pigment in the scalp to look like tiny hair follicles, giving the appearance of a close-cropped head or greater density. It is also used to conceal hair transplant scars and scars from burns or injuries.

In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as an alternative to hair transplants or hair systems for men who prefer a buzzed look. Published clinical evidence was not found; Wikipedia's article relies on news and magazine sources.
quick.mechanism: Pigment is placed superficially in the epidermis and upper dermis, with color matched to the person's hair. Treatment typically takes three to four sessions of about two hours.
quick.risks: Poor technique can produce an unnatural hairline. Practitioners may patch-test for ink allergy. Wikipedia reports that the result is permanent but can be removed by laser, and notes that its statement about no scientific data on side effects lacks a citation.

lead: Scalp micropigmentation (SMP), also called a hair tattoo, is a non-surgical cosmetic tattoo that makes a bald or thinning scalp look like a close buzz cut or gives the impression of more density.[1] It can also conceal hair transplant scars and burn or other scars on the head.[1]

Pigment is deposited into the scalp to mimic tiny hair follicles, more superficially than a traditional tattoo.[1] The article on Wikipedia cites no clinical studies; its sources are news and magazine pieces from 2012 onward.[1] In looksmaxxing forums it is compared with hair transplants and hair systems.
infobox: Three to four sessions of about two hours

paras: The pigment color is matched to the person's current hair color, and the hairline is described as among the most important parts of the treatment.[1] A patch test may be performed to check for ink allergy.[1] When done well the result can look natural; a poorly executed hairline can look unnatural, though it can be adjusted or touched up.[1]

Wikipedia names poor technique as the main concern and says that, with ink from a reputable distributor, there are no scientific data on side effects over ten years; that statement is flagged as needing a citation.[1] The pigment can be removed by laser.[1]
No studies found. No clinical trial of scalp micropigmentation appeared in the sources reviewed.

lore.intro: Forum users compare SMP with hair transplants and hair systems, mostly for men who wear a shaved style.[2][3]

claims.claim: SMP only suits men who keep a bald or buzzed look.
claims.believers: A looksmax.org user says it helps only for those who always wear a bald look, have visible gaps from a failed transplant, or have diffuse thinning, and that it does little for typical male pattern baldness; he favors hair systems.[2]
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes the procedure as imitating a buzz cut or added density and as camouflage for scars; it reports no regrowth effect.[1]

claims.claim: A hair transplant may be preferable to SMP if the person wants natural hair length.
claims.believers: In another thread a user is advised to get a transplant to restore temple peaks, while the poster wants to keep a buzzcut length.[3]
claims.experts: No published studies compare SMP and transplants in the sources reviewed.
